messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1 — GPU pool effective capacity degradation detected: pool=pool-rt-us-west, reported_available=60%, observed_latency_spike, paging @ashley :rotating_light:

ashley: Taking the pager. Seeing sustained queue growth on /v1/generate. Token service shows backlog ~1200 reqs, median queue time ~35s, 429 and 503 counts increasing. Attaching quick logs below.

ashley: logs:
```
[14:02:11Z] driver=nv-kmod id=gpu-42 status=OOM Xid=79 state=unresponsive
[14:02:13Z] poolctl: evict attempt failed: node gpu-node-17 reporting 'ghost' capacity
[14:02:20Z] autoscaler: attempted scale-up blocked by quota_limit (max_nodes=200)
[14:02:30Z] service: route latency > 2s, 5xx count +18% over 5m
```

raj: Copy. Looking at node health now. `nvidia-smi` on gpu-node-17 returns no processes but kernel shows Xid errors and kernel driver in weird state. Hypothesis: intermittent driver OOM/XID causing node to be marked unhealthy, autoscaler doesn't reclaim because node still reports some GPUs present -> 'ghost' capacity.

tess: Confirmed. Kube shows node not Ready but not fully removed: pods stuck Terminating with finalizers. Autoscaler sees capacity but runtime not usable. Queue builds because routing prefers the pool.

raj: Immediate mitigations I'm proposing (fast):
- evict affected node from pool to force replace: `poolctl mark-unhealthy --node=gpu-node-17 --force`
- allow autoscaler to allocate new nodes: bump soft cap for pool-rt-us-west by 3 transient nodes `poolctl quota set pool-rt-us-west --soft+3`
- create temporary routing rule to failover low-latency traffic to small-quant model: `route set /v1/generate --fallback-model=redwood/quant-small --percent=30`

ashley: Doing mark-unhealthy now. Running `poolctl mark-unhealthy --node=gpu-node-17 --force` -> response: node state transition queued. Kicking drain on the node.

tess: Starting `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — some pods stuck on finalizers (csi, kubelet). Escalating to infra-sre for node-level reset.

infra-sre: I'm on it. From host: seeing repeated kernel messages: `NVRM: Xid (0x4b)`, and modprobe rmmod fails because device busy. Plan: 1) gracefully restart kubelet so pod termination proceeds; 2) attempt driver reload: `sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia` then `systemctl start kubelet`. If that fails, we will hard-reboot via IPMI.

pm-anna: Customer impact: a few larger customers on the real-time tier are seeing elevated latency and some dropped requests. Support has flagged two accounts (acct-alpha, acct-gamma) with measurable error spikes. We should notify them we're migrating traffic to fallback models and adding capacity.

ashley: Executing driver reload procedure on gpu-node-17 now. Watch: `sudo modprobe -r nvidia` -> fails (device busy). Proceeding to stop kubelet.

raj: While that's happening, I'm requesting a transient quota increase with cloud team to let autoscaler add nodes. Pasting request: `REQ: +4 GPU nodes in us-west-2 until 2026-03-15T16:00Z — urgency: high — reason: pool ghosting prevents reclamation`

oncall-bot: NOTE: autoscaler attempted 3 scale-up actions; cloud quota prevented allocation. Manual quota increase in progress.

tess: kubelet stopped, re-running `modprobe -r nvidia` -> still complaining about device busy referencing nvidia-persistenced. Killing persisting processes: `pkill -f nvidia-persistenced`. Retry unload -> success. Reload driver -> success. Starting kubelet.

ashley: Node rejoined Ready but runtime reports reduced GPUs: gpu-node-17 now reports 2/4 GPUs healthy. Some pods recovered.

raj: Good. For nodes that still show partial capacity we should avoid routing heavy traffic until full pass. I'm applying a routing policy to exclude nodes reporting <100% health: `poolctl set-routing-policy --pool=pool-rt-us-west --min-gpu-health=100` this will divert requests away from degraded nodes.

ashley: Implemented. Traffic dropped to fallback model for 30% of requests. Queue decreased from 1200 -> 300 in 12 minutes. Latency trending back to normal. :thumbsup:

infra-sre: Cloud team granted temporary +3 nodes. Autoscaler added 3 nodes, pool capacity up to 92% effective. Monitoring for kernel Xid recurrence.

pm-anna: Notifying affected customers: sending note about degraded service and remediation in progress, offering status updates.

ashley: Quick customer-impact summary for incident notes:
- impact window start: 2026-03-15T14:00Z
- observed effects: increased queueing, 429/503 responses, higher generation latency for real-time tier customers (not all customers affected)
- mitigation: force-unhealthy node mark, driver reload and node reboot as needed, transient quota increase + autoscaler additions, routing to fallback quantized model (30%)
- status now: degraded -> recovering, pool effective capacity ~92%, queue draining.

raj: Next actions (post-incident):
- run kernel/driver forensic on gpu-node-17: capture dmesg, hardware logs, nvidia diagnostics
- evaluate autoscaler logic: ensure nodes in 'ghost' state don't block scale-up decisions; add explicit check for runtime health in addition to node reported capacity
- add runbook step to temporarily route percent to fallback model automatically when queue > 500 and capacity < 70%

tess: I'm taking notes for the postmortem. Also raising a ticket to fleet team to validate node firmware on gpu-node-17 class.

ashley: Handoff: handing to leo for 30m watch and post-incident checks. `@leo` please watch pool-rt-us-west, confirm no Xid recurrence, follow-up with cloud quota rollback when safe.

leo: Ack — taking over. I'll watch telemetry and prepare a brief pager follow-up.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: severity downgraded to P2 at 2026-03-15T14:42Z, oncall handoff to leo.

ashley: Thanks team. Postmortem requested, tagging infra-sre and eng-runtime.

pm-anna: I'll draft the customer update and coordinate with support.

raj: quick note: we should add an automated health probe into autoscaler: if driver reports Xid or OOM within last 10m, treat node as unusable even if K8s reports capacity. Filing RFC.
